name: Commodore VIC-20
description: Commodore's first colour home computer, sold in Japan as the VIC-1001 in 1980 and worldwide from 1981. It was cheap, sold in toy and department stores, and advertised by William Shatner. It was the first computer to sell a million units.

specs.memory: 5 KB RAM (3.5 KB free for BASIC)

curiosities: William Shatner starred in its TV advertising.
It was sold as the VC-20 in Germany, marketed as a "Volkscomputer".
It was the first computer of any kind to sell one million units.
Its text screen was only 22 characters wide.
story: Commodore wanted a colour computer for under $300. Built around MOS's VIC chip, the VIC-20 launched in Japan as the VIC-1001 in 1980 and worldwide in 1981.

William Shatner sold it on television as 'the wonder computer of the 1980s'. With 5 KB of memory and 22 columns of text it was modest, but it was sold in toy and department stores, not only computer shops, and games came on cartridges and tapes.
It became the first computer to sell a million units, and opened the way for the Commodore 64 that replaced it.
